title: Regional continuity broker for streamed sessions and active-active traffic steering
creator: Alice Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a regional continuity broker in the hosted API gateway that enables active-active traffic steering while preserving session/stream continuity for streaming RPCs and long-lived sessions. The broker should allow fast traffic shifts between regions without client-visible truncation or duplicate tokens, support circuit breakers and load-shedding policies per-region, and integrate with existing KV cache sync and prefix-caching heuristics.

Context: We already have multi-region gateways and session affinity primitives, but heavy region-to-region shifts cause state gaps for streaming sessions (lost final tokens, retransmit ambiguity, inconsistent KV caches). This work creates a coordination layer that mediates handover (graceful switch), enforces region circuit-break thresholds, and applies per-request hedging/fallbacks to meet SLOs (p95 tail latency and success rate targets).
acceptance_criteria: Broker routes a session-level handover such that a client streaming session can be resumed in target region without data loss in >=95% of planned cutovers during canary traffic
p95 end-to-end request latency from edge to first model token remains within 1.2x baseline for regional fallback flows under normal load
Circuit breaker triggers when region error-rate > 4% over a 30s sliding window and prevents >90% of new ingress requests from being routed to that region
Load-shedding policy reduces inflight concurrency for affected region by at least 60% within 10s of threshold breach
KV prefix-cache resynchronization reduces cache-miss induced cold-start token overhead by >=40% compared to naive fallback in lab tests
Comprehensive e2e tests and chaos scenarios included in CI and the playbook for on-call runbook
Rollout can be toggled via feature flag and rolled back without client-side changes
technical_design:
High level: introduce a lightweight regional continuity broker component co-located with the gateway control plane. Responsibilities:
- Maintain soft session ownership metadata (session_id -> active_region, last_applied_seq, kv-sync-token) in a strongly-consistent store for short retention (TTL 60s) to avoid long-lived global locks.
- Provide an RPC for handover that accepts a resume token and last_applied_seq; broker validates continuity and issues a transient resume grant.
- Implement two handover modes: fast-hedge (send duplicate request to target region + respond to client from first responder) and state-forwarding (transfer small session state via the control plane for sessions with >10s idle threshold).
- Circuit breaker: fast-moving sliding-window monitor with three states (Closed, Degraded, Open) per region and per-model; thresholds and cooldowns configurable via console.
- Load-shedding: token-bucket-style admission per region; priority queues for system-level vs best-effort traffic. Admission interacts with batching logic to avoid starving small requests.
- KV cache sync: use incremental delta sync where possible; broker stores short-lifetime KV manifests for hot prefixes to accelerate target region warmup.
- Telemetry: emit per-session handover events, reason codes (owner-drain, region-error, capacity-shed), and pre/post-handshake latency histograms.

Implementation notes: keep broker stateless for long-term durability—state is in the control plane store (existing Dynamo-style store). Use gRPC streaming for fast handshake; reuse existing session IDs and resume semantics from gateway. Avoid adding new client-visible headers unless necessary; prefer transient resume tokens validated server-side.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag and canary: ship broker behind a runtime feature flag default-off. Enable for 1% of traffic to target region A for 48 hours. 2) Canary expansion: ramp to 10%, 25%, 50% with automated checks on handover success rate and p95 latency. 3) Wide rollout: enable for all traffic after two successful 48-hour canaries. 4) Controlled failover test: run scheduled cross-region drain exercises during a low-traffic window and validate session continuity metrics. 5) Post-rollout: monitor for 2 weeks; then flip default to on and move flag to console-only.
Rollback criteria: handover success <90% at canary or p95 latency exceeds baseline by >30% for 15+ minutes. Quick rollback via feature flag toggle and immediate re-route to previous steering policy.
metrics_and_slo:
Primary SLOs: 
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful responses (2xx/stream-ok) for hosted API global.
- Continuity SLO for streaming sessions: 99.0% of planned region shifts must resume without token/data loss.
- Latency SLO: p95 first-token latency must remain <= baseline * 1.2 for normal fallback flows.
Observed metrics to emit: handover_attempts, handover_success_rate, handover_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, region_error_rate_30s, region_circuit_state, admission_rejection_rate, kv_warmup_time, duplicate-response-rate (hedge hits).
Alerting: Pager when handover_success_rate < 90% for 5 minutes or region_error_rate_30s > 6% or admission_rejection_rate > 10% for 10 minutes.
Dashboards: add per-region heatmap (handover rate vs success rate) and model-specific gating charts.
test_plan: Unit tests for broker state transitions and transient resume token validation
Integration tests: end-to-end streaming session hugged across two regions in staging with synthetic client harness (including network partitions and delayed packets)
Chaos testing: automated scenario that kills a region gateway mid-stream and measures handover continuity under controlled load
Performance benchmarking: measure p50/p95/p99 latency for handover path vs baseline for small/medium/large batch sizes
Canary observability smoke tests that fail the CI if any handover metric drops below threshold
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Duplicate tokens or double-delivery when hedging first-responder wins. Mitigation: broker marks hedged requests and enforces idempotent resume grants; client SDK guidance to dedupe events for a short window.
Risk: Write amplification on KV sync for very large prefix sets. Mitigation: cap prefix manifest size and fall back to on-demand warming; use sampling and LRU heuristics.
Risk: Increased control-plane load and latency. Mitigation: limit broker TTL and use batched writes to control-store; provision autoscaling for control plane.
Risk: Mis-configured circuit thresholds causing premature open state. Mitigation: provide conservative defaults, staged tuning, and a safety override in the console for operators.
Risk: Behavior differences between models with very different decode characteristics. Mitigation: model-level circuit and admission policies; run per-model canaries before global enablement.
notes: 2026-03-01: Spike showed state-forwarding adds ~12ms median during handover for large sessions; decided to prefer fast-hedge for <5s idle sessions.
2026-03-04: Ops requested a per-customer override to disable hedging; added as a follow-up subtask.
2026-03-08: Telemetry schema agreed with Observability team; added duplicate-response-rate metric to the contract.
Next steps: implement gRPC handshake, wire control-store bindings, and add console knobs for thresholds. Coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer-facing messaging.
